name: oxframe
description: Make videos from code with oxframe: explainers, code walkthroughs, charts, matrices, 3D, slides and release videos as Rust scenes, checked with `oxframe check` (storyboard and report) and rendered to MP4 without a browser. Use when the user asks for an animation, a motion graphic, a video from code, or changes to an oxframe project.
html:
oxframe scenes

The project is on oxframe 0.23.8: docs https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.23, model text https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.23/llms.txt (and https://oxframe.dev/docs/0.23/llms-full.txt), API https://docs.rs/oxframe/0.23.8/oxframe/. oxframe mcp exposes check, inspect, render_graph, render_frame and docs_search. oxframe --json check prints one JSON object.

No project yet

When the user wants a video and there is no oxframe project (no oxframe.toml):

  1. Install the CLI: curl -fsSL https://github.com/oxygenframe/oxframe-cli/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh (or cargo install oxframe-cli). Rendering needs ffmpeg.
  2. oxframe init my-video creates the project: src/main.rs with one scene, oxframe.toml, and this skill with project notes in AGENTS.md.
  3. cd my-video, write the scenes, then follow the workflow below. oxframe render writes out/my-video.mp4.

Rust is needed on the machine, but the user does not need to know it: the scenes are short async functions, and oxframe check tells you what is wrong.

Workflow

  1. Read src/main.rs and the scene's src/<scene>.meta.json (markers/tunables already tuned by a human — keep them).
  2. Make the change. Prefer small, readable steps: one .await per beat of the story, all((..)) for things that happen together.
  3. oxframe check. Fix compile errors first (see AGENTS.md, "Common compile errors"). Then open out/check/storyboard.png and out/check/report.json. Each issue names a rule, a time range, a node and file:line. An issue on a node also has crop, a close-up PNG under out/check/issues/ with the node outlined: open it. Most issues carry fix, the change with the numbers worked out (move by dx/dy px, shrink, a text color, widen by px or font_scale, hold or slow in seconds): start from it, and keep the design in mind (moving a title 140 px may call for moving its neighbours too).
  4. Fix and run oxframe check again until it exits 0. Warnings do not fail the command; errors do.
  5. oxframe inspect --at <t> when a frame looks wrong and you need the node tree (kind, name, bounds, text). Add --graph to see render passes. oxframe snapshot --at <t> for one full-size still.
  6. Only then report. Mention the storyboard and which issues you fixed.

Never run oxframe dev (interactive server). Never hand-edit meta.json unless asked.

When the user asks for a link to the video, oxframe publish --title "…" renders it and prints a public oxframe.dev link (30 days, up to 30 s: --range 0..30). Never publish unasked: anyone with the link can watch.

API

The full cheat sheet is in reference.md: nodes and their properties, flow functions, easing, signals, text, layout, effects, meta helpers.

Recipes

Reach for the right node before writing the scene:

  • Explaining code (what an expression does, why a line matters, a bug fix): a Code node is the tool, not plain Txt. Show the source, then walk attention through it with .focus(first, last) or .focus_lines(a, b, secs) and .dim(0.3) on the rest; to explain parts of one expression, focus each column range in turn. Morph to the next version with .code().to(next, secs), or use .insert/.remove/.replace. For a line-by-line walkthrough with a note per step, CodeExplainer::new(src).step(line, line, "note").
  • Vertical (9:16) or square short: Project::new(..).size(1080, 1920) for portrait, (1080, 1080) for square — or Project::aspects([Aspect::Portrait]) and oxframe render --aspect 9:16. view.is_portrait() adapts the layout.
  • Charts and math: Axes/NumberLine with .plot(..), bars, scatter; Matrix, axes.vector(..). A title, bullets or an end card: the components (TitleCard, BulletList, EndCard), not hand-placed Txt.

name: chart-video
description: Animate data as a video: bars that grow, line series, a dot riding a curve, a sorted table, axes that zoom. Use for data stories, benchmark results, bar chart races or turning numbers into a short clip.
html:
Uses the oxframe skill (workflow, full API cheat sheet); install both with npx skills add oxygenframe/oxframe-sdk.

#[oxframe::scene]
async fn benchmark(view: View) {
    view.add(Txt::new().text("Frame time, ms").h2().to_edge(Edge::Top));
    let axes = view.add(Axes::new().x_range(-0.5..3.5).y_range(0.0..20.0));
    let bars = axes.bars([0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0]).labels(["vello", "skia", "cairo", "wgpu"]);
    for (i, v) in [4.0, 12.0, 18.0, 3.0].into_iter().enumerate() {
        bars.value(i).to(v, 0.8).await;
    }
    wait_for(1.5).await;
}
  • Bars: set the x range to -0.5..n - 0.5; bars.value(i) is a signal, bars.bar(i) the rectangle (color it to highlight).
  • Lines: axes.line_series([(x, y), …]) (each point is a signal), dots: axes.scatter([…]). Zoom with axes.x_range().to(a..b, secs).
  • Rankings: Table::new(["Name", "Time"]).row([..]), then insert_row, sort_by_column(c, secs) and row(i).background().fade_in() for the winner.
  • There is no pie chart: draw slices with Custom and ctx.arc.
  • Numbers on screen must come from the data the user gave; do not invent values.

name: code-walkthrough
description: Explain a piece of code step by step in a video: highlight lines, show a note for each step, then morph the code into its next version. Use for tutorials, onboarding videos, or explaining an algorithm's code.
html:
Uses the oxframe skill (workflow, full API cheat sheet); install both with npx skills add oxygenframe/oxframe-sdk.

const SRC: &str = "fn search(xs: &[i32], x: i32) -> Option<usize> {\n    let (mut lo, mut hi) = (0, xs.len());\n    while lo < hi {\n        let mid = (lo + hi) / 2;\n        if xs[mid] < x { lo = mid + 1 } else { hi = mid }\n    }\n    (lo < xs.len() && xs[lo] == x).then_some(lo)\n}";

#[oxframe::scene]
async fn walkthrough(view: View) {
    let card = view.add(TitleCard::new("Binary search").subtitle("in eight lines"));
    card.enter().await;
    card.next().await;
    wait_for(1.0).await;
    card.exit().await;
    let explain = view.add(
        CodeExplainer::new(SRC)
            .step(2, 2, "Search the whole slice")
            .step(4, 4, "Look at the middle")
            .step(5, 5, "Drop the half that cannot hold x")
            .step(7, 7, "Found, or not"),
    );
    explain.enter().await;
    for _ in 0..4 {
        explain.next().await;
        wait_for(2.0).await;
    }
}
  • One idea per step, a short note (under 8 words), 2 s or more per step so check does not report too_fast.
  • For a free layout use a Code node with .focus_lines(a, b, secs) and a Callout::new(node).text("…"), or morph versions with .code().to(next, secs).
  • Pair it with a diagram (FlowDiagram) or a chart when the code does something visual.

name: manim-to-oxframe
description: Port a Manim (Python) scene to oxframe (Rust): construct, self.play with Create/FadeIn/Transform, Axes and plots, ValueTracker, NumberPlane and apply_matrix, Matrix, 3D. Use when migrating from Manim CE or ManimGL or making 3Blue1Brown-style videos without Python.
html:
Uses the oxframe skill (workflow, full API cheat sheet); install both with npx skills add oxygenframe/oxframe-sdk.

Manimoxframe
class S(Scene): def construct(self):#[oxframe::scene] async fn s(view: View)
self.play(Create(circle))let c = view.add(Circle::new().size(200.0)); c.draw_on().await;
self.play(FadeIn(m)) / FadeOutm.fade_in().await / m.fade_out().await
self.play(a.animate.shift(RIGHT))a.x().to(a.x().get() + 100.0, 1.0).await
self.play(A, B)all((a, b)).await
self.wait(1)wait_for(1.0).await
Transform(text_a, text_b)txt.morph_to("new text", 1.0).await
Text("Hi")Txt::new().text("Hi").h1()
MathTex(r"\frac{a}{b}")not yet: Unicode in Txt (a/b, √x, x²)
Axes(x_range=[-3, 3]), axes.plot(lambda x: …)Axes::new().x_range(-3.0..3.0), axes.plot(|x| …)
ValueTracker(0), always_redrawSignal::new(0.0), .bind(move || …) or axes.point_on(&plot, x)
NumberPlane(), apply_matrix(m)Axes::new(), axes.apply_matrix([[a, b], [c, d]], secs)
Vector([1, 2])axes.vector(1.0, 2.0)
Matrix([[1, 2], [3, 4]])Matrix::new([[1, 2], [3, 4]]) (row_frame, cell)
ThreeDSceneScene3d + View3d (feature 3d)
self.camera.frame.animate.scale(0.5)Camera node: camera.zoom().to(2.0, 1.0)
manim -pqh scene.py Soxframe render (oxframe dev for a live editor)

No Cairo, Pango or LaTeX to install, and the browser playground at oxframe.dev runs the same scenes. Keep Manim's pacing: one animation per .await, short waits between ideas, then oxframe check.

name: math-explainer
description: Make a math or algorithm explainer video in the style of 3Blue1Brown with oxframe: axes and function plots, a dot riding a curve, vectors and linear maps, matrices step by step. Use for math animation, visual proofs, linear algebra or calculus explainers.
html:
Uses the oxframe skill (workflow, full API cheat sheet); install both with npx skills add oxygenframe/oxframe-sdk.

#[oxframe::scene]
async fn derivative(view: View) {
    let axes = view.add(Axes::new().x_range(-3.0..3.0).y_range(-1.5..1.5));
    let f = axes.plot(|x| x.sin());
    f.draw_on().await;
    let x = Signal::new(-3.0);
    axes.point_on(&f, x.clone());
    x.to(3.0, 3.0).await;
    f.to_fn(|x| x.cos(), 1.0).await;          // morph into the derivative
}
  • Functions: axes.plot(|x| …) follows the ranges (axes.x_range().to(..) zooms) and keeps gaps (tan). point_on, to_fn, axes.place(node, x, y).
  • Linear algebra: axes.vector(x, y) (tip is signals), axes.apply_matrix([[a, b], [c, d]], secs) bends the grid and everything on it; Matrix::new([[1, 2], [3, 4]]) with row_frame, column_frame, cell(r, c) to point at entries.
  • Number lines and bars: NumberLine::new(0.0..10.0), axes.bars([..]).
  • 3D surfaces or solids: Scene3d + View3d (feature 3d).
  • Formulas: there is no LaTeX/Typst yet. Write short expressions with Unicode (f′(x) = cos x, ∑, √, superscripts) in Txt, or as matrix cells.
  • Pace like the classics: one idea, one motion, a pause (wait_for) to let it land.

name: motion-canvas-to-oxframe
description: Port a Motion Canvas project (TypeScript generators) to oxframe (Rust async): makeScene2D, yield*, all/chain, refs, signals, waitUntil and transitions mapped one to one. Use when migrating from Motion Canvas or Revideo.
html:
Uses the oxframe skill (workflow, full API cheat sheet); install both with npx skills add oxygenframe/oxframe-sdk.

The model is the same: a scene is code that runs over time, nodes have signal properties, and the editor retimes marked moments. Generators become async.

Motion Canvasoxframe
makeScene2D(function* (view) { … })#[oxframe::scene] async fn name(view: View) { … }
view.add(<Rect ref={r} width={200} fill="#e13238" />)let r = view.add(Rect::new().width(200.0).fill(color!("#e13238")));
yield* r().x(300, 1)r.x().to(300.0, 1.0).await
yield* all(a, b)all((a, b)).await
yield* chain(a, b) / sequence(0.1, …)a.await; b.await; / stagger(0.1, items, |x| …)
yield* waitFor(1)wait_for(1.0).await
yield* waitUntil('event')wait_until("event").await (a marker in meta.json)
createSignal(0)Signal::new(0.0); derived: Signal::derived(|| …)
yield r().x(300, 1) in parallelspawn(async move { … })
<Layout direction="column" gap={20}>Layout::new().direction(Direction::Column).gap(20.0)
<Txt text="Hi" fontSize={80} />Txt::new().text("Hi").font_size(80.0)
<Code code={…} />, code().code(next, 1)Code::new().code(src), code.code().to(next, 1.0)
slideTransition(Direction.Left)transition(Transition::slide(Dir::Left)).await
easeInOutCubicpresets::IN_OUT_CUBIC or ease!("name") (editable)
npm run serve / renderoxframe dev / oxframe render (server-side, no browser)

Port scene by scene: keep the structure of yield* lines as .await lines, convert refs to the handles view.add returns, then oxframe check.

name: oxframe-check
description: Read and fix `oxframe check` reports: storyboard.png and report.json with named rules (out_of_frame, text_overflow, too_fast, low_contrast, dead_time…). Use after any change to an oxframe scene, or when check exits 1.
html:
Uses the oxframe skill (workflow, full API cheat sheet); install both with npx skills add oxygenframe/oxframe-sdk.

oxframe check type-checks the project, runs every scene and writes out/check/storyboard.png and out/check/report.json. It exits 1 on errors; warnings do not fail it. oxframe --json check prints the report on stdout.

Each issue has rule, severity, a time range, a node, file:line and (from oxframe 0.20.1) docs, a link to the rule's section of https://oxframe.dev/docs/check-rules with a before and after picture. An issue tied to one node also has bounds, its pixel rect [x0, y0, x1, y1] at the start of the range, and (from oxframe 0.21) crop, a full-resolution PNG of that part of the frame with the node outlined in red, relative to out/check/ (for example issues/01-out_of_frame.png). Open the crop to see the problem up close instead of finding it on the storyboard. Fix errors first, then warnings, then run check again until it exits 0. Look at the storyboard before reporting: a clean report is necessary, not sufficient.

RuleWhat it meansUsual fix
out_of_frameA node leaves the frame or the safe areaSmaller size, pct(), to_edge(Edge::…), or move the camera
text_overflowText wider than its box or the frameShorter text, .caption()/.body() instead of a heading, a wider box
text_overlapText on top of textnext_to, a Layout, or fade one out first
covers_textA shader drawn over textAdd the shader before the text, or move the text out of its box
low_contrastText too close to its backgroundA theme role: .fill(Text) on Surface, OnAccent on Accent
too_fastText not on screen long enough to read, or a large move too quickwait_for(…) after it appears, a longer tween
dead_timeNothing changes for too longShorten the wait or animate something
voice_cut / voice_overlapA spoken line runs past the scene, or two lines overlapline.await before the scene ends; start the next line after
shader_error, param_unknown, shader_slow, input_cycleShader problemsSee the Shaders section of the cheat sheet
nondeterministicTwo paints of one frame differDraw only from signals and ctx.time(); randomness from ctx.rng(seed)
video_unavailableA clip cannot be openedCheck the path and the video feature; install ffmpeg

report.json also lists motion: every node that travels, when it moves (moves, in seconds), where it starts and ends, and its file:line; read it to check timing ("does the title arrive before the voice says its name?") without watching the video. out/check/trajectories/<scene>.png draws those paths over the scene's last frame, numbered as in motion.

To see what an edit changed, keep the frames from before it and compare: oxframe check --frames --out out/before, edit, then oxframe check --against out/before. Each changed frame is listed with the share of pixels that moved and a diff/ picture (changed pixels in red); an edit that changed frames it should not have shows up at once. Hard cuts between scenes appear on the storyboard as the last frame of one scene and the first of the next.

oxframe inspect --at <seconds> prints the node tree (kind, name, bounds, text) when the picture is unclear; --graph adds the render passes. oxframe snapshot --at <seconds> writes one full-size frame. Thresholds live in oxframe.toml under [check]; change them only when the user asks.

name: pr-to-video
description: Animate a pull request or a code change as a short video: the old code morphs into the new one token by token, with the changed lines in focus. Use for PR summaries, code review videos, or 'show what changed' requests.
html:
Uses the oxframe skill (workflow, full API cheat sheet); install both with npx skills add oxygenframe/oxframe-sdk.

Get the change with git diff or gh pr diff <n>. Show each changed file (or the one that matters) as a Code node, then animate it to the new version: .code().to(..) diffs tokens, so kept code stays and changed code moves, appears or fades.

const BEFORE: &str = "fn total(items: &[Item]) -> u32 {\n    items.iter().map(|i| i.price).sum()\n}";
const AFTER: &str = "fn total(items: &[Item]) -> u32 {\n    items.iter().filter(|i| i.in_stock).map(|i| i.price).sum()\n}";

#[oxframe::scene]
async fn change(view: View) {
    view.add(Txt::new().text("Skip items out of stock").h2().to_edge(Edge::Top));
    let code = view.add(Code::new().code(BEFORE).language("rust"));
    wait_for(1.0).await;
    code.focus_lines(2, 2, 0.4).await;
    code.code().to(AFTER, 1.2).flash().await;
    wait_for(1.5).await;
}
  • .insert(line, col, text, secs), .remove(((l, c), (l, c)), secs) and .replace(range, text, secs) edit in place; lines are 1-based, columns 0-based.
  • One file per scene, about 20 lines on screen; cut the rest from the snippet. Long files: .focus(first, last) and .dim(0.3).
  • Use CodeExplainer::new(src).step(first, last, "what it does") when the video should walk through the new code instead of the change.

name: release-to-video
description: Turn release notes or a changelog into a short video: title card with the version, the changes as lists, an end card. Use for release announcements, changelog videos, or setting up oxygenframe/release-video-action in CI.
html:
Uses the oxframe skill (workflow, full API cheat sheet); install both with npx skills add oxygenframe/oxframe-sdk.

In CI, with no code

on:
  release:
    types: [published]
jobs:
  video:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: oxygenframe/release-video-action@v1

The action turns headings into title cards and bullets into lists, runs oxframe check, renders with --cpu and attaches release.mp4 to the release. A release created by a workflow with GITHUB_TOKEN does not trigger on: release: add the step to that job with tag: ${{ github.ref_name }}. portrait: true renders 9:16; credit: false drops "made with oxframe".

As a scene of your own

#[oxframe::scene]
async fn release(view: View) {
    let title = view.add(TitleCard::new("v2.4.0").subtitle("What's new"));
    title.enter().await;
    title.next().await;
    wait_for(1.5).await;
    title.exit().await;
    let changes = view.add(BulletList::new(["Faster startup", "Dark theme", "Bug fixes"]));
    changes.enter().await;
    for _ in 0..3 {
        changes.next().await;
        wait_for(1.2).await;
    }
    changes.exit().await;
    let end = view.add(EndCard::new("Update now").note("example.com"));
    end.enter().await;
    end.next().await;
    wait_for(1.0).await;
}

Keep one idea per card and at most five bullets per list; split longer sections into several lists. Hold each card long enough to read, or oxframe check reports too_fast.

name: remotion-to-oxframe
description: Port a Remotion (React) video to oxframe (Rust): compositions, useCurrentFrame/interpolate, Sequence, spring, Img/Video/Audio and rendering mapped to oxframe scenes and signals. Use when migrating from Remotion or comparing the two.
html:
Uses the oxframe skill (workflow, full API cheat sheet); install both with npx skills add oxygenframe/oxframe-sdk.

Remotion computes every frame from useCurrentFrame(). oxframe runs a scene as an async fn where each .await takes time, and values are signals that .to(target, seconds) animates. Port the timeline, not the per-frame math.

Remotionoxframe
<Composition durationInFrames fps width height>Project::new("name").fps(60).size(1920, 1080).scene(main()); length comes from the scene
useCurrentFrame() + interpolate(frame, [0, 30], [0, 1])node.opacity().to(1.0, 0.5).await
spring()an ease: .to(v, 0.6).ease(presets::OUT_BACK)
<Sequence from={30}>wait_for(0.5).await before it, spawn(async { … }) to run alongside, or another scene
<AbsoluteFill>the View; Layout for flex rows and columns
<Img>, <Video>, <Audio>Img, Video (feature video), sound("x.wav").play() / Audio::track(..)
staticFile("logo.svg")Svg::new().file("assets/logo.svg") (or include_bytes!)
CSS / Tailwind stylingthe theme: Accent, Surface, .h1(), .radius(Lg)
<TransitionSeries>transition(Transition::fade()).await at the start of the next scene
npx remotion renderoxframe render (no browser; --jobs for parallel segments)
Remotion LambdaCI on a plain runner; --cpu needs no GPU

Steps: list the compositions and their sequences, write one oxframe scene per composition (or per major sequence), port timings in seconds (frames / fps), replace styled boxes with components (TitleCard, BulletList, LowerThird, EndCard) where they fit, then oxframe check and compare frames with oxframe snapshot --at <s>.

License note for the user: oxframe is MIT/Apache-2.0 with no seat or render fees.

name: slides
description: Turn oxframe scenes into a presentation: stops on click, speaker notes in a presenter window, slide clickers, and a PDF of every stop. Use for talks, conference slides, or 'make this video a presentation' requests.
html:
Uses the oxframe skill (workflow, full API cheat sheet); install both with npx skills add oxygenframe/oxframe-sdk.

#[oxframe::scene]
async fn opening(view: View) {
    notes("Introduce yourself.");
    let title = view.add(TitleCard::new("Video as code"));
    title.enter().await;
    wait_for(1.5).await;
    slide_break().await;

    notes("One point per click.");
    let points = view.add(BulletList::new(["Scenes are async Rust", "Every value is a signal"]));
    points.enter().await;
    for _ in 0..2 {
        points.next().await;
        wait_for(1.5).await;
        slide_break().await;
    }
}
  • slide_break().await is a stop; the end of every scene is one too. A render plays straight through, so hold with wait_for before each break (or check reports too_fast). Do not fade out the last point; the next scene's transition takes it away.
  • notes("…") belong to the part that ends at the next stop.
  • oxframe present opens the talk full screen: → / space / PageDown next, ← / PageUp back, F full screen, N the notes window with a timer.
  • oxframe render --slides talk.pdf writes one page per stop.

name: voiceover
description: Add narration to an oxframe video and sync the animation to spoken words: voice lines, waiting for a word, ducking music, subtitles, a text-to-speech provider. Use for narrated explainers, voiceovers or captions.
html:
Uses the oxframe skill (workflow, full API cheat sheet); install both with npx skills add oxygenframe/oxframe-sdk.

#[oxframe::scene]
async fn intro(view: View) {
    let square = view.add(Rect::new().size(200.0).fill(Accent).opacity(0.0));
    let line = voice("First we draw a square, then we turn it").start();
    line.at_word("square").await;
    square.fade_in().await;
    line.at_word("turn").await;
    square.rotation().to(90.0, 1.0).await;
    line.await;                       // the scene must not end before the line
}
  • voice(text).start() speaks now; .at_word("word") waits for that word; awaiting the line waits for its end. check reports voice_cut and voice_overlap.
  • oxframe does not call a speech service. Implement TtsProvider (id, synthesize → Synthesis { rate, samples, words }) and pass it with Project::tts(..); read the API key from the environment. Without a provider or key, timing is estimated and there is no audio.
  • The first render caches audio in tts/; commit that folder so CI renders the real voice without a key.
  • Music: Project::audio(Audio::track("assets/music.mp3").duck_under_voice()).
  • Subtitles: oxframe render --subtitles out.srt (.vtt by extension).
